stimulus.source_note: Theodor de Bry, engraving of Indigenous workers in the Potosi silver mine, 1590, public domain; the image is a European engraving made by an artist who never visited the Americas.
stimulus.text: The engraving shows Indigenous workers inside the silver mine at Potosi, in the Andes mountains of South America. Workers climb ladders carrying baskets of ore on their backs, while others break rock with tools below. Spanish overseers stand among them. The mine opened in 1545 and became the richest source of silver in the Spanish Empire.

stem: The engraving was made by Theodor de Bry, a European artist who never visited the Americas. Which statement best describes how a historian should use this image as evidence about labor in the Potosi mines?

options.text: The image is useless as evidence because de Bry never saw the mines himself.
options.misconception: A source made at a distance is limited, not useless; it still shows how Europeans pictured the mines.

options.text: The image proves that Indigenous workers welcomed Spanish rule in the mines.
options.misconception: Nothing in the image shows willing workers; it shows forced labor under overseers.

options.text: The image shows the mine's labor system, but its details need checking against other sources.
The image proves that Spanish overseers did the mining work alongside Indigenous laborers.
options.misconception: The overseers in the image watch and direct the work; the workers carry the ore.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
